title: bonsai.bugs/1
description: The bugs page (contract §7.3, §7.5; plan P-T-6023): one row per bug, built from the bug files (bonsai.bug/1), for a person to read on one page. It lives at the place bonsai.yaml names under documents.bugs (work/bugs.md when absent), the path the project's old hand-kept register had, so links to it keep working. Generated: written only by bonsai check --write, in the main checkout, and only while the file is missing or carries this format line (the generated marker); a page without it, a register not moved yet, is left as it is and named by the warning bugs-not-moved. Read by people, agents and the studio, which knows by its format to read the bug files instead. The bug files stay the truth: nothing reads the page to decide, and it grants nothing. A page that differs from a rebuild is the warning tables, never a finding. A markdown file whose frontmatter holds format and whose body holds the rest; a JSON Schema cannot describe a markdown table, so this schema describes what a reader returns (the frontmatter's fields, then what it reads from the body), and the body's lines and column order are formats/README.md's. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version line, the frontmatter's only key (contract §2.2); it carries a comment saying the file is generated and never edited by hand. It is the generated marker: a page whose format line is not bonsai.bugs/ (a hand-kept register, before its project moved it to bug files) is never overwritten by check --write and is an ordinary file to the guard and to rung 0.

bugs.description: One row per bug file in the project's bug folder that parses, grouped by status, the open ones first (open, watched, fixed, wontfix: the sections Open, Watched, Fixed and Won't fix), newest id first in each (by its number); [] for none. A bug file that does not parse under its format gives no row: check reports it as a finding.

examples.title: The sessions cache's version number is not tied to the build

examples: The sessions cache's version number is not tied to the build

status.description: The bug's status, read from the section its row is in: bonsai.bug/1's closed list (its one home, bug.schema.json).

area.description: Its area, or null for none.

where.description: Where it goes wrong, or null.

found_by.description: Who or what found it, or null.

fixed_in.description: The commit or commits that fixed it, or null.

task.description: The task that fixed it, or null.

closed.description: The day it was fixed or set wontfix, as its file gives it (YYYY-MM-DD, the UTC day, contract §23); null while it is open or watched, or when an old register named no day.

why.description: Why it is wontfix or watched, or null.
